newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs end mostly up, bellies fall on technicals.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs end mostly up, bellies fall on technicals.

text.p: CME hog futures closed mostly higher on "bargain hunting" while pork bellies fell as cash concerns pushed prices down through technical support and touched off sell stops, traders said.

Hogs ended off 0.100 cent per lb to up 0.300 cent with only April off at 69.075 cents. Pork bellies closed 2.075 to 1.675 cent a lb lower in 1997 contracts with May off most at 74.425. Newly listed 1998 contracts rose the 3.000-cent limit in thin trade.
Sources noted that hog prices have come down enough in the past month to look like a bargain, which supported hog futures, but overhead resistance continued on weak cash markets, they said.
"We tried for weeks to come up with some reason to rally this market and we just can't find a reason," said Dave Maher with Securities Corp of Iowa.

Maher noted that cash pork prices have been pressured by a lack of retailer demand and this is keeping futures from rallying as many traders had anticipated. Further losses in most pork cuts at noon and calls for steady to lower cash hogs Thursday added to pressure in April, they said.
Rolling of long fund positions into back months also kept April down while supporting June. Deferred months ended up on projections of lower hog supplies this summer, they added.

Rand Financials was a light buyer early but turned seller along with LFG in April midsession with Refco again selling April and buying June late. Cargill Investor Services was on the other side. In hog options, Iowa sold April 68 puts early. Commission houses sold 68 to 72 puts and bought 70 to 75 calls in April. Volatility was firm, pit sources said.

Pork belly futures tumbled late as pressure from weak fundamentals pushed prices through major technical support and touched off sell stops. Futures were pressured from the start by Tuesday's bearish CME out-of-town report, traders said.
"The Out-of-Town was negative - we had an in-movement this year going against an out-movement last year" in the weekly report, Maher said.

Concern that product was going into storage instead of being taken by users. Futures are high enough to encourage some basis trade and the storage report already showed a growing amount of certified deliverable stocks, they said.

But technically-sparked fund selling was responsible for pushing prices down to day's lows late. Prudential Securities and E.D.& F. Man notably sold on the break while R.J. O'Brien and RBH bought, pit sources said.
